items.title: Anthropic shipped faster Claude 5.2 models
items.oneliner: Anthropic says Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 are 30% faster and cheaper, pushing frontier performance toward production reality.

items.title: Meta released its cheapest serious reasoning model
items.oneliner: Meta's Muse Ember matches Claude Haiku-class scores at roughly one-third the cost, raising the floor for agent economics.

items.title: An AI model helped crack a quantum conjecture
items.oneliner: Psi says an Anthropic model found a proof for the 18-year-old Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture after three days of autonomous search.

items.title: Coding agents still fail most real edits
items.oneliner: Co-Design Bench found the best coding agent fully solved just 26.4% of 273 real app-editing tasks.

items.title: Terminal2Shell exposed instant shell access
items.oneliner: Terminal2Shell claims a cross-platform input-validation flaw can hand attackers instant shell access on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

items.title: Qubole trust relationships became an attack path
items.oneliner: Attackers used Qubole's trusted roles to reach customer data, reminding every platform team that vendor access is production access.

items.title: Gemini can route personal files to reviewers
items.oneliner: Google's updated Gemini policies now allow personal Gmail, Docs, and Drive content to reach human annotators.

items.title: Microsoft quietly made DMARC effectively mandatory
items.oneliner: Microsoft started rejecting mail without DMARC, even with SPF and DKIM, turning email hygiene into a deliverability outage.

items.title: PyPI added clearer package security signals
items.oneliner: PyPI's redesigned project pages now surface provenance and attestation status, making package trust easier to evaluate before install.

items.title: Anthropic is buying its own power supply
items.oneliner: Anthropic reportedly locked up 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generation, proving AI infrastructure bottlenecks now start at the grid.
